correctness.rationale: For \(\lvert z\rvert\le R<1\), the complex-analytic identity \(\lvert\operatorname{sech}^2(sz)\rvert\le\sec^2(sR)\) implies \(\lvert\tanh z\rvert\le(\tan R/R)\lvert z\rvert\). The synchronized boundary \(z=iR\) realizes equality. Maximal-modulus radial comparison proves forward invariance exactly when \(\delta=\alpha-\beta\tan R/R\ge0\), with a nonzero equilibrium at equality. For \(\delta>0\), the maximum modulus decreases at least as \(e^{-\delta t}\). The real part of the derivative is at most \(1+(\tan R/R)^2\lvert z\rvert^2\) above its linear value, so the graph Rayleigh inequality gives a disagreement logarithmic derivative bound \(-\rho+\beta\tan^2R\,e^{-2\delta t}\), where \(\rho=\alpha-\beta+\kappa\lambda_2\). The integrated bound supplies the finite prefactor. An arbitrarily small Fiedler-mode initial condition has a nonzero limiting rescaled projection \(e^{\rho t}\langle v,Pz(t)\rangle\) by an explicitly integrable cubic perturbation. This excludes all uniformly larger exponents. Bi-Lipschitz comparison of disc-Kobayashi distances and Euclidean distances transfers the result to the intrinsic metric. Independent symbolic equalities and a finite standard-library numerical check are included; the infinite quantifiers follow from proof, not testing.

value.rationale: The motivating article explicitly identifies a large discrepancy between a provably safe contraction bound and numerically observed rate and calls for a network-aware spectral estimate. This theorem resolves the sharp nonlinear all-data rate and its uniform transient prefactor, proves that no faster universal exponent is possible, and derives an exact maximal-disc design boundary with a critical family of stationary obstructions. These are structural, parameter-explicit synchronization guarantees useful for complex coupled networks beyond just a numerical linearization. No assertion of general arbitrary holomorphic system or publication-scale contribution is needed.
